cols.text: Each row shows one layout in four frames, left to right: writing an equation, finding a symbol, after Copy, and the 820 px pop-out window. The first three are the side panel at 400 px. Styling is plain grey on purpose.

capA.text:
A – Stage and dock
The equation takes the top third. Copy stays pinned at the bottom. Symbols sit between.

capB.text:
B – Tabs
Symbols, Draw, Library and Shortcuts are four tabs under the equation. Nothing hides in a menu.

capC.text:
C – One box
One search box finds symbols, saved equations and commands. Only recent symbols show until you type.

capD.text:
D – Keyboard
A maths keypad is docked at the bottom like a phone keyboard. Copy sits in the top bar.

capE.text:
E – Rail
Tools live on a side rail that is always visible. The window gets a labelled sidebar and two columns.

capF.text:
F – Scratchpad
A running list of equations. Each line copies with one press, and old lines stay for reuse.

headB.text: Layout B, Copy formats and skip links

colsB.text: Each row shows B with one way to handle Copy formats: writing, after Copy, changing the format, and the pop-out window. The last row shows where skip links could go.

capB0.text:
B1 – Two buttons
Both formats are one press away. Your main format is the large button and Alt+C.

capB1.text:
B2 – Split button
One button copies your main format. The arrow opens the other and can swap them.

capB2.text:
B3 – Format switch
One Copy button with a LaTeX or MathML switch beside it. The switch stays where you leave it.

capB3.text:
B4 – One button
The panel asks once which format you paste. Only that format shows, and Settings changes it.

capB4.text:
Skip links
Left to right: a bar on the first Tab press, a link before the symbols, a link after them, and F6 between regions.
